connection_model: OneCrew records are local. Outreach derives its operator from the selected route or conversation; use each operation's exact input and connection contract.
gotchas: Ask user questions with onecrew.ask_user_question and consume completed answers once. Answers clarify intent; they do not approve an unrelated downstream write.
Do not merge identities from display names alone.
Present result_ref for the user's App confirmation of the held payload without refetching, then read back saved Creators. Choice answers are not save authority.
Each confirmation authorizes one frozen call. Batches reuse result_ref for later reviews and keep completed receipts; only final status resumes the model.
Only onecrew.creator.export XLSX is canonical; map CSV or other sheets into explicit onecrew.creator.batch.create items and reject missing or ambiguous fields.
Owner statuses: eligible_new, eligible_update, existing_skipped, duplicate_skipped, identity_pending, contact_conflict, failed; count eligible_new toward a new Creator target.
identifier_semantics: OneCrew record IDs are durable local identities and are not provider handles.
Candidate explicit intent (add_new/save_or_update), target, connection, provenance, notes, tags and quality; batches use one intent and no candidate cache.
Historical discovery and candidate IDs stay provenance; current reads return provider IDs. Use actual row_id values for reviews and outcomes.
onecrew.creator.candidate.batch.save takes one candidates array, up to 50; the eight-call envelope and provider concurrency are separate limits.
A link hub found in any profile is read with onecrew.link_hub.extract: links and emails return as found; nothing is saved until a Creator save confirms them.
Owner preparation reads fresh profiles and hubs, writes no Creator rows or reservations, and holds the immutable typed payload in the result owner.
